After importation the whole ginger is inspected, cleaned if necessary and ground at Kalustyan Corporation’s plant in Union, New Jersey. reasoning: At issue is whether the ground ginger qualifies for preferential NAFTA tariff treatment under the NAFTA Rules of Origin Regulations. Due to amendments to the 2012 Customs Tariff, subheading 0910.10 is now a suppressed subheading that has been further subdivided into subheadings 0910.11 and 0910.12. facts: This wall-mounted (recessed) niche features a toilet paper holder, a storage shelf, a door with storage tray for a garbage can, a toilet brush and a reusable bottle with sprayer. This good is wholly produced in China from Chinese materials. The product is packaged in a cardboard box.
reasoning: According to Schedule I, paragraph 1(6) of the Determination of Country of Origin for the Purpose of Marking Goods (Non-CUSMA Countries) Regulations, the brush is the only item covered by the marking rules. However, according to Schedule II, paragraph 14 of the Regulations, the brush is exempt from marking when it is in a container that is marked in a manner that will reasonably indicate its origin to the ultimate purchaser.
